Add JavaFX GUI for TA Terror (Level 9/10) and fix chat bubble rendering
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements Main/Launcher/MainWindow/DialogBox on top of the existing
TATerror CLI, using the existing Duke-style tutorial pattern.

Two bugs were found and fixed after the initial GUI implementation:

1. Chat bubbles were completely invisible (zero height). DialogBox.fxml's
   root HBox had prefHeight="-Infinity", which in JavaFX is a special
   sentinel (USE_PREF_SIZE) valid for min/maxHeight but meaningless when
   applied to prefHeight itself - it resolved to a preferred height of 0,
   collapsing every dialog row regardless of its child Label's actual
   size/text/color. Removed prefHeight="-Infinity" so it auto-computes
   from children as intended; minHeight/maxHeight="-Infinity" now
   correctly lock onto that computed value.

2. main.css used a `*` wildcard selector to paint every node's background
   dark, which fought with dialog-box.css's per-bubble colors depending on
   cascade resolution. Scoped it to `.root, .anchor-pane` instead so only
   the window background is set globally, leaving DialogBox's own
   stylesheet in full control of bubble colors.

Also increased the ScrollPane's top anchor (1px -> 15px) so the first
message isn't flush against the window's top edge.

Verified via debug instrumentation (temporary, removed) showing the
HBox height went from 0.0 to a correct computed value, and via a live
run showing multi-turn conversation rendering with readable bubbles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Untrack data/ - it's runtime save data, not source
commitResults.messageBody:
Stop tracking data/tasks.txt in git and ignore the whole data/ folder.

Reason: the file was tracked from an old commit, so a `git reset --hard`
(needed to redo the A-Gradle merge properly) silently reverted a
teammate's real saved tasks back to a stale committed version, wiping
out entries added since. Untracking it means git operations on source
history can no longer touch it either way.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for TATerror.getResponse (A-JUnit)
commitResults.messageBody:
9 test methods covering distinct validation/parsing branches inside
getResponse(): bye, unrecognized command, mark with a non-numeric
index, mark with an out-of-range index, todo/deadline/event missing
required parts, find without a keyword, and the list command's
response header.

Deliberately scoped to inputs that never reach saveTasks() (no
successful todo/deadline/event/mark/unmark/delete), so running the
suite can never overwrite data/tasks.txt - doubly safe now that
data/ is also gitignored (see previous commit).

The other classes (Main, Launcher, MainWindow, DialogBox) are pure
JavaFX plumbing that needs the JavaFX Application Thread booted to
construct anything meaningfully - not attempting that here to keep
this increment's scope minimal and reliable, per the course's stated
"at least two non-trivial methods, tested reasonably well" bar, which
this suite comfortably exceeds within TATerror alone.

Verified: `./gradlew test` -> 9/9 passing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-JavaDoc into master
Extract Task/TaskList/Storage/Parser/Ui out of TATerror (A-MoreOOP)
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the parallel-array task representation (descriptions[], isDone[],
types[], byRaw[], fromRaw[], toRaw[]) with a proper object model, and pulls
TATerror's four separate responsibilities apart into their own classes:

- Task (abstract) + Todo/Deadline/Event: each task's own type code, save
  format, and display formatting live with the type itself via polymorphism
  (toSaveDetail()/toDisplayDetail()/toString()), instead of formatTask()
  switching on a type-code string.
- TaskList: owns the actual List<Task> and its operations (add/remove/get/
  isValidIndex/findByKeyword).
- Storage: load()/save() - the file I/O and pipe-format (de)serialization,
  now parameterized by file path instead of a hardcoded constant.
- Parser: command recognition (isXCommand) and argument extraction
  (parseTaskIndex/parseArguments/splitDeadlineArgs/splitEventArgs),
  replacing the inline startsWith/substring logic.
- Ui: the CLI-only banner/prompt/divider printing used by main(), so the
  JavaFX GUI's own presentation classes (MainWindow, DialogBox) aren't
  the only "view" layer in the codebase.

TATerror.getResponse() is now a thin coordinator: ask Parser to recognize
+ extract, tell TaskList/Task to act, tell Storage to persist, format the
reply. Its public API (constructor, getResponse(String)) is unchanged, so
MainWindow/DialogBox/Main/Launcher needed no changes.

Deliberately behavior-preserving, not a rewrite - this replicates the
original's exact (sometimes inconsistent) parsing quirks, e.g. todo/find
trim() their extracted argument but deadline/event don't, matching the
original bug-for-bug rather than "fixing" it as a side effect of this
refactor.

Verified:
- `./gradlew test`: all 9 existing TATerrorTest cases pass unchanged,
  exercising the same input/output pairs against the new code path.
- Manual CLI smoke test in an isolated temp dir (todo/deadline/event/
  list/mark/delete/find/bye) produces identical output and an identical
  save-file format to before.
- `./gradlew run`: GUI still launches cleanly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-MoreOOP into master
Organize classes into packages (A-Packages)
commitResults.messageBody:
Went for the stretch goal (multiple packages by concern, matching the
course's own duke.task/duke.command example) rather than the minimal
single-package option, since A-MoreOOP just gave this codebase 13
classes with natural groupings:

- taterror            TATerror (coordinator/facade), Main, Launcher
- taterror.task       Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList
- taterror.storage    Storage
- taterror.parser     Parser
- taterror.ui         Ui (CLI-only)
- taterror.gui        MainWindow, DialogBox (JavaFX-only)

src/main/java remains the source root (not itself turned into
packages), per the course's explicit instruction.

Two non-obvious things this touches beyond simple file moves + package
declarations:
- MainWindow.fxml's fx:controller="MainWindow" -> "taterror.gui.MainWindow" -
  FXML resolves the controller class by name, so this would have silently
  broken GUI loading at runtime (ClassNotFoundException) if left as-is.
  DialogBox.fxml needed no change since DialogBox sets itself as
  controller/root in code rather than being named in the FXML.
- build.gradle's application.mainClass: 'Launcher' -> 'taterror.Launcher'.

Also moved src/test/java/TATerrorTest.java to src/test/java/taterror/
with a matching package declaration, and fixed a stale saveTasks()
reference in its class doc comment (renamed to Storage.save() during
A-MoreOOP but missed at the time).

Verified: `./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava` succeeds, all 9 tests
still pass, `./gradlew run` launches the GUI cleanly (confirming the
fx:controller fix actually resolves), and both the shadow jar and the
CLI (`java -cp ... taterror.TATerror`) still work correctly run from a
clean isolated directory - same behavior and save-file format as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-A-Packages into master
Comply with SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Several public methods/constructors were missing header
comments, and a few method summaries didn't start with a verb
(e.g. "The raw ... text" instead of "Returns the raw ... text").

The SE-EDU Java coding standard requires Javadoc on all public
classes/methods (getters/setters excepted), with summaries
starting in the form "Returns...", "Sends...", "Adds...", etc.

Let's add the missing comments (Task.markAsDone/markAsNotDone,
the Todo/Deadline/Event constructors, Storage's and Ui's
constructors, TaskList.add) and rephrase the non-verb-first
summaries (Task's abstract methods, Deadline.getByRaw,
TaskList.isValidIndex/asList, MainWindow.initialize/
handleUserInput) into the required form.

Also swaps an inline fully-qualified java.io.File.separator
reference in TATerror for a proper import, per "imported
classes should always be listed explicitly."

Verified: gradlew test still passes all 9 cases, and gradlew
run still launches cleanly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
